title: Family, and the Oldest Words We Have
label: ch:family
canDo: I can name the four closest family members in French, each with its article, and use one sound-law to recognise their English cousins.

payoff.summary: Four words — père, mère, frère, sœur — and every one of them is older than Latin. Each also hands you an English word you already knew: paternal, maternal, fraternal, sorority. One sound-law, Grimm's p→f and t→th, turns père into father and frāter into brother in a single move, and the fused letter œ arrives here and waits in cœur, œuf and œil.
payoff.note: Authored when chapter 12 left the hand-written set: two schema-v1 lessons held four headwords between them, so each word, the sound-law the .tex hid in a grammarlens, and the œ ligature now own a lesson each. The payoff is atom-scored -- it assesses every atom its chapter introduces.
